title: Clopen partitions on a w-local affine scheme
statement:
The patch topology of an affine scheme is compact Hausdorff. For a w-local
[def-weil-pbc-w-local] affine scheme $X$, its closed point set $X^c$ is a
profinite space, and restriction identifies clopen partitions of $X$ with
clopen partitions of $X^c$. An open subset containing a part of $X^c$
contains the corresponding components of $X$.

proof.text: For X = PrimeSpectrum A, Mathlib supplies spectrality and compactness of the constructible topology. A compact open is both open and closed constructibly. Use the compact-open basis to refine an open distinguishing two points (T0), then take the compact open or its complement as appropriate. Thus the constructible topology is totally separated and Hausdorff. Transfer to WithConstructibleTopology by its continuous injective identity map.

The source-library instances WLocalSpace.spectralSpace_closedPoints, WLocalSpace.t1Space_closedPoints and WLocalSpace.CompactSpace_closedPoints make the closed-point subspace spectral, T1 and compact. SpectralSpace.totallySeparatedSpace then gives Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness. These instances are already proved, with only standard axioms.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-w-local-closed-points-components-homeomorphism]. Write e for the canonical homeomorphism from closed points to connected components and r(x) = e^{-1}([x]). The map r is continuous, r(c) = c for closed points, and r(x) lies in the component of x. For every clopen U, connected-component containment gives x in U if and only if r(x) in U.

For a partition (P_i) of the closed-point subspace, set Q_i = r^{-1}(P_i). Continuity gives clopenness, inverse images preserve disjointness and arbitrary unions, and r(c)=c gives the prescribed restriction. Any other clopen lift Q_i' satisfies x in Q_i' iff r(x) in Q_i' iff r(x) in P_i iff x in Q_i, proving uniqueness. Conversely, pullback along the closed-point inclusion preserves clopenness, disjointness and the union. This also treats empty index sets and empty spectra; no finite-support argument is needed.

For x in the component of a closed point c, use exists_isClosed_specializes to choose a closed specialization d of x. Specialization preserves the connected-component class. Injectivity of the canonical closed-point map identifies d with c. Hence x specializes to c, and every open containing c contains x. Apply to c in E and the given image inclusion.
